{{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = [[Governor of Montana|Governor]] | before_election = [[Greg Gianforte]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Greg Gianforte]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 76.57%{{decrease}}4.76{{cite web |url=https://electionresults.mt.gov/VoterTurnoutDetails.aspx|title=Montana Voter Turnout|newspaper=Montana Secretary of State - Christi Jacobsen|date=19 December 2024 |access-date=2025-07-23}} }} {{Elections in Montana}} The '''2024 Montana gubernatorial election''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect the [[governor of Montana|governor]] of the U.S. state of [[Montana]], concurrently with the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 U.S. presidential election]], as well as [[2024 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]], elections to the [[United States House of Representatives]], and various [[2024 United States elections#State elections|state]] and local elections. Primary elections took place on June 4, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-08-06 |publisher=[[National Conference of State Legislatures]]}} Incumbent [[Montana Republican Party|Republican]] Governor [[Greg Gianforte]] won election to a second term, defeating [[Montana Democratic Party|Democratic]] nominee Ryan Busse. Gianforte won by a 20% margin, which was larger than his 13% margin in [[2020 Montana gubernatorial election|2020]].{{Cite web |date=2024-06-05 |title=Busse and Gianforte win their respective primary races |url=https://www.krtv.com/news/montana-politics/busse-and-gianforte-win-their-respective-primary-races |access-date=2024-10-27 |website=KRTV NEWS Great Falls |language=en}} Though Montana has backed Republicans in every presidential election since [[1996 United States presidential election in Montana|1996]], the sparsely populated [[Mountain state]] maintained a Democratic tendency at the state and U.S. Senate levels well through the 2010s. This was the first gubernatorial election since [[1996 Montana gubernatorial election|1996]] that a Republican was re-elected governor of Montana. This was also the largest margin of victory in a gubernatorial election since [[Brian Schweitzer]]'s 33-point re-election victory in [[2008 Montana gubernatorial election|2008]], and the largest for a Republican since [[Mark Racicot]]'s aforementioned 58-point landslide re-election in [[1996 Montana gubernatorial election|1996]]. {{toclimit|4}} ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== *[[Greg Gianforte]], incumbent governor (2021–present){{cite news |work=[[KFYR-TV]] |access-date=January 17, 2024 |url=https://www.kfyrtv.com/2024/01/17/governor-greg-gianforte-seek-reelection/ |date=January 17, 2024 |author=Anthony, Michael |title=Governor Greg Gianforte to seek reelection}} **Running mate: [[Kristen Juras]], incumbent lieutenant governor (2021–present) ==== Eliminated in primary ==== *[[Tanner Smith (politician)|Tanner Smith]], [[Montana House of Representatives|state representative]] (2023–present){{cite web |last1=Larson |first1=Seaborn |title=Freshman GOP Rep. announces run for governor |url=https://helenair.com/news/state-regional/government-politics/tanner-smith-candidate-for-montana-governor/article_cb34eb00-0a0b-11ee-afe3-b7a14a35295c.html |website=[[Independent Record]] |date=13 June 2023}} **Running mate: Randy Pinocci, member of the [[Montana Public Service Commission]] (2019–present){{Cite web |author1=Kimbel-Sannit, Arren |author2=Sakariassen, Alex |author3=Eggert, Amanda |date=2024-04-15 |title=Who's running for office in Montana's 2024 election |url=http://montanafreepress.org/2024/04/15/whos-running-state-federal-office-montana-2024-election/ |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=[[Montana Free Press]] |language=en-US}} === Endorsements === {{Endorsements box|title=Greg Gianforte|list=;Organizations *[[National Rifle Association Political Victory Fund]]{{Cite web |last=NRA-PVF |title=NRA-PVF {{!}} Grades {{!}} Montana |url=https://www.nrapvf.org/grades/montana |access-date=2024-05-13 |website=NRA-PVF |language=en}} *[[Susan B.
